summary.headline: Prime Fresh Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.7% to INR81.71 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to INR6 crore (9.83% margin), which management says is not fully sustainable.
summary.overview: Prime Fresh reported Q1 FY27 sales of INR81.71 crore (vs INR53.34 crore), EBITDA of INR6 crore (9.83% margin vs 7.53%) and PAT of INR4.35 crore (vs INR2.89 crore). Management attributed part of the jump to one-off recoveries of pending service-business billings, inventory gains from rising F&V and onion prices, and strong service volumes, and guided that margins may not be sustained. Forward guidance is EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and volume growth of 15% to 25%, with value growth of 25% to 30%. The company is pursuing the Nashik cluster development project under the National Horticulture Board, expected to be awarded in August 2026, and a Bank of Baroda working capital limit increase to INR20 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Bank of Baroda cash credit limit
financial_highlights.change: Raised from INR7.8 crore at 8.5% cost

segments.name: F&V business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Management stated FY23 sales of about INR275 crore, of which about INR245 crore plus came from F&V and the balance from service business. B2C is 1% to 2% of business; exports stopped post-COVID.

segments.name: Service business
segments.commentary: Q1 saw good volume growth and strong margins, plus recovery of old pending billings that aided the quarter. Management said this contribution is not expected to recur at the same level.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Florens Farming Ltd is the key focus for own farming and land tie-ups; management said it contributes about 10% of F&V and could pay off from next year. Prime Fresh Retail India Pvt Ltd is held for strategic partners; B2C entry deferred.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 7.5%; net profit margin guidance stated as 5.5% to 5% (as transcribed, likely a typo).
Volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum in one answer and 15% to 25% in closing remarks; value growth of 25% to 30%.
Internal aspiration of 9.5% to 11% EBITDA margin in 2 to 2.5 years (around 2029) and a vision of INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031; longer-term EBITDA margin of 14% to 16% in 4 to 5 years.
Operating margin expected to rise slowly from mid-FY28.
Debtor target of 88 to 94 days of sales, debtors below 25% of sales, and no single rupee of working capital or equity needed for an incremental INR60 crore sale by FY29.
Product portfolio to add three to four more categories within a year (currently 9 to 12 F&V products).
capex_capacity: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board: company as implementing agency; expected award in August 2026; INR75 crore investment (excluding INR5-6 crore preoperative spend), of which INR50-52 crore eligible for 40-50% grant (about INR24 crore grant expected on milestones).
Capex to start around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18 to 20 months; Phase 1 INR6-9 crore, Phase 2 INR12-15 crore, balance in Phase 3, funded from own balance sheet including debt.
Project debt peak about INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned, falling to INR18-20 crore after grants.
Farmer component of about INR60 crore with around 35% government subsidy; target of 15,000 farmers and 15,000 tons incremental sourcing in year 1, scaling to 2 lakh tons in six years.
Sourcing capacity close to 2.5 lakh tons vs FY sales of about 65,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Customer mix: about 20 large modern trade and e-commerce accounts, around 90 APMC partners, 10 to 15 food processors, 20 to 30 exporters; added four to five food processing customers in Q1.
Price pass-through of 4 to 8 days on procurement changes for most business; HoReCa about one month; 5-star and tender business up to 3 months, which is under 4% of business.
Pomegranate: about 13,000 farmers and 40 plus local area aggregators; onion prices rising sharply, benefiting inventory gains.
Procurement advantage of direct farm sourcing stated at 3% to 15% on price, with 10% to 15% operational cost initially; long-term advantage 5% to 8% over supplier purchase.
Company is positioned as a pan-India supplier to modern trade and e-commerce across 10 cities for onion, pomegranate and orange.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables (about one-third of revenue) be reduced and can trade payables be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a client credit exposure system, stricter onboarding with PDCs and security cheques, and about INR12 crore debtor reduction in Q1. It aims at 88-94 debtor days and a 25% of sales cap; a BoB limit rise to INR20 crore plus INR20 crore for Nashik was cited; payables to farmers are expected to rise to INR10-15 crore on credit by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Nashik Sinnar project add beyond the asset-light model?
qa_highlights.answer: Prime Fresh is implementing agency for a farmer component (subsidy-led) and an IA component of INR75 crore with 40-50% grant on eligible capex; it aims at order-book model, farm-gate packhouse and cold chain, and a separate call was offered.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative capex, revenue/tonnage and margin impact, and replication to other cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex over about 18-20 months with phased balance-sheet spend; quantified margin uplift not given. Replication via subsidiary or SPV route is open, with full equity payback in up to 5 years targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Lag between procurement price changes and customer price resets?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 4 to 8 days; HoReCa up to one month; tender business up to three months, under 4% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 trading and direct expenses up faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the numbers and said it would respond by mail.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter B2C given the city footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C needs heavy upfront investment; an earlier franchise attempt cost INR55-75 lakh in 2021-2023. Management decided not to pursue it now, with B2C at 1-2% of business.

risks_watch: Receivables still about one-third of revenue; management targets 88-94 debtor days and debtors below 25% of sales, with INR7-8 crore of legacy slow/non-moving debtors (FY22-FY25) still to collect. Track monthly debtor days and collections.

Management itself flagged Q1 margins (9.83% EBITDA) as not fully sustainable, citing one-off recoveries of old service billings and inventory gains; guidance reverts to 7%-7.5% EBITDA margin. Watch for normalisation in Q2.
Trading and direct expenses rose faster than revenue in Q1; management did not have the breakdown on the call and promised a reply by mail. Confirm the reply and the cause of the cost increase.

Nashik (Sinnar) cluster project: award expected in August 2026, capex from around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18-20 months, INR75 crore IA investment with about INR24 crore grant on milestones; project debt peaks near INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned. Track award, grant receipts and execution delays.
Guidance inconsistencies in the transcript: net profit margin given as 5.5% to 5% and volume growth as 15%-20% minimum in one answer vs 15%-25% in closing remarks. Clarify before modelling.

Long-term targets (9.5%-11% EBITDA margin around 2029, INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031, 14%-16% margin in 4-5 years) are aspirational with no quantified margin bridge; the Nashik margin uplift was not quantified.
key_quotes: Going forward, these margins may not be sustainable because of a couple of reasons for this substantial jump has come during quarter one.

So, our internal target is definitely to go to 88 days to 94 days, you know, as a percentage of sales, and we should be able to have at least 4x, you know, sales of, you know, our outstanding debtors and not have debtors beyond 25% of sales.
So, let me get back to numbers, and we will mail you.
So, these consistent efforts will make sure that our volume growth always remains between 15% to 25% as we speak.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, the Nashik project and the working capital turnaround, citing the BoB limit increase and debtor reduction. It was cautious on sustainability of Q1 margins, which it said would not hold, and evasive on the trading and direct expense question, deferring it to a mail reply.

adds.what: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board, INR75 crore investment (excl. INR5-6 crore preoperative)

growth.why: Management guides value growth of 25% to 30% and volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum for FY27, with the INR75 crore Nashik cluster project expected to be awarded August 2026 and capex starting end-October to end-November 2026, though management cautioned Q1 profit boosts (one-off recoveries, inventory gains) are not sustainable and no capacity utilisation figure was given.
